work: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books I-VII + VIII-XV

items.name: the Gorgon's head
items.description: Medusa's severed head, which Perseus uses to turn Atlas, Phineus, Polydectes and others to stone.

items.name: the Horn of Plenty
items.description: The horn Hercules tore from Acheloüs, filled by the Naiads with fruit and flowers.

wikipedia.lead: In classical antiquity, the cornucopia, also called the horn of plenty, is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts. In Greek, it was called the horn of Amalthea (Ancient Greek: κέρας Ἀμαλθείας, romanized: kéras Amaltheías), after Amalthea, a nurse of Zeus, who is often part of stories of the horn's origin.

items.name: Jupiter's thunderbolt
items.description: Jupiter's weapon, used against the Giants, Phaëton and Semele.

wikipedia.lead: A thunderbolt, or lightning bolt, is a symbolic representation of lightning. It appears variously in history, literature, and in contemporary warnings of (typically high-voltage) electricity.

items.name: the javelin of Cephalus
items.description: Unerring javelin given by Procris, which Cephalus unwittingly uses to kill her.

items.name: the wings of Dædalus
items.description: Wings of feathers, thread and wax, built to escape Crete; Icarus falls when the wax melts.

items.name: the Golden Fleece
items.description: The fleece of the ram kept in Colchis, which the Argonauts sail to fetch and Jason wins with Medea's help.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Golden Fleece is the fleece of the golden-woolled, winged ram, Chrysomallos, which rescued Phrixus and brought him to Colchis, where Phrixus then sacrificed it to Zeus. Phrixus gave the fleece to King Aeëtes, who kept it in a sacred grove, whence Jason and the Argonauts stole it with the help of Medea, Aeëtes's daughter.

items.name: Ariadne's crown
items.description: Crown thrown by Liber into the heavens, where its jewels become stars.

wikipedia.lead: Corona Borealis is a small constellation in the Northern Celestial Hemisphere. It is one of the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century astronomer Ptolemy, and remains one of the 88 modern constellations.

items.name: the shield of Achilles
items.description: Achilles' armour and shield, contested by Ajax and Ulysses and awarded to Ulysses.

wikipedia.lead: The shield of Achilles is the shield that Achilles uses in his fight with Hector, as described in a passage in Book 18, lines 478–608 of Homer's Iliad. The intricately detailed imagery on the shield has inspired many different interpretations of its significance.

items.name: the tunic of Nessus
items.description: Centaur Nessus's blood-poisoned robe, sent by Deïanira to Hercules, whose burning agony leads to his death.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Shirt of Nessus, Tunic of Nessus, Nessus-robe, or Nessus' shirt was the poisoned shirt (chiton) that killed Heracles. It was once a popular reference in literature.

items.name: the trident
items.description: Neptune's three-pronged weapon, which he strikes on the earth to release the flood and lays aside to end it.

wikipedia.lead: The trident of Poseidon and his Roman equivalent, Neptune, has been their traditional divine attribute in many ancient depictions. Poseidon's trident was crafted by the Cyclopes.

items.name: the lock of Nisus
items.description: The purple lock guarding Nisus's kingdom, cut by Scylla for love of Minos.

items.name: the Palladium
items.description: The stolen statue of Minerva Ulysses cites among his deeds.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, the Palladium or Palladion was a cult image of great antiquity on which the safety of Troy and later Rome was said to depend, the wooden statue (xoanon) of Pallas Athena that Odysseus and Diomedes stole from the citadel of Troy and which was later taken to the future site of Rome by Aeneas. The Roman story is related in Virgil's Aeneid and other works.

items.name: the golden apples
items.description: Three apples given by Venus, thrown by Hippomenes to delay Atalanta and win the race.

items.name: Ceres' girdle
items.description: Girdle of Proserpina, brought up by Cyane's pool, which shows Ceres her daughter's fate.

items.name: Pygmalion's statue
items.description: The ivory woman Pygmalion carves and loves, brought to life by Venus.

items.name: Vulcan's net
items.description: A fine net forged by Vulcan to trap Venus and Mars in adultery.

items.name: the brand of Meleager
items.description: The log tied to Meleager's life by the Fates, burned by his mother Althæa.

items.name: the goblet of Anius
items.description: Carved goblet given to Aeneas, showing Orion's daughters sacrificing themselves.

items.name: the golden branch
items.description: The branch pointed out by the Sibyl to Aeneas for his journey into the underworld.

wikipedia.lead: The Golden Bough is a fantastical object described in the Aeneid, an epic poem by the Roman poet Virgil composed between 29 and 19 BC narrating the adventures of the Trojan hero Aeneas after the Trojan War. The episode of the Golden Bough is found in its sixth book and is part of Aeneas's journey into the Underworld.

items.name: the herb moly
items.description: Herb given by Mercury to Ulysses to resist Circe's enchantments.

items.name: the ivory shoulder of Pelops
items.description: Ivory replacement for the shoulder lost when Pelops was cut apart.

items.name: the veil of Thisbe
items.description: Veil dropped when fleeing the lioness, found bloodied by Pyramus, who kills himself.
